texts: An old woman was struggling alone on the road with her bags and nobody stopped to help; I want a poem about not walking past someone in need.
doha on being kind to people who are suffering
pity for the suffering
I want a doha that tells us where there is compassion there is dharma, and that anyone who turns away from a person in pain has lost the very root of religion, no matter how many prayers he says.
Where tenderness for the afflicted lives, there righteousness has made its dwelling.
moon, gentle mercy
Under the moon last night I sat with a crying stranger at the station and listened until dawn, and it felt like the best thing I have done this year.

Compose a doha showing that kindness to the weak is like the moon giving cool light to everyone alike, and that a person's greatness is measured by how gently he treats those who have nothing to give back.
The moon pours coolness on the poor and the rich alike; so flows mercy from the tender soul.
doha on kindness to everyone like the moon shining on all

Write me a doha about how the strong should protect the weak and the healthy should comfort the sick, because a person who has no pity for the suffering has already lost his claim to be called a human being.
care for the weak
doha on helping people who are down
When my neighbour lost her job, I made her a meal every day for a month; it was the only thing I could do and it mattered.
Lift the fallen with a gentle hand, and heaven bows its head to you.
The jaggery of kindness melts upon the bitter day, and a diamond of mercy outshines every crown.
Could you write a doha about how a little jaggery given with love to a hungry child is worth more than a diamond hoarded by a hard-hearted man, since mercy shared is the only true wealth we carry?
My grandfather once gave his last piece of jaggery to a starving boy at the station, though he owned a diamond ring, and never regretted it.
doha on giving jaggery to the hungry, kindness more than a diamond
jaggery, diamond, mercy
At the foot of the mountain near the cremation ground, a woman sat alone mourning her husband, and the village women came one by one to sit beside her without saying anything.
mountain, cremation ground, comfort
doha on comforting someone grieving, w mountain and cremation ground
Compose a doha about those who stand beside a grieving soul at the cremation ground below a silent mountain, offering nothing but presence, and how that tenderness is the highest form of religion.
Below the mountain's silence, at the cremation ground, kind hearts keep company with the broken.
Please write a doha about how a kind word and helping hand offered to a poor person in the market is worth more than a hundred rituals, because kindness to the helpless is the real worship of God.
At the market a boy with no shoes stood staring at the sweets, and an old man bought him some without a word; I could not forget it.
market, kindness to poor
Amid the noise of the market let one hand reach out in tenderness; that is the true prayer.
doha on being kind to poor kids at the market

Please write a doha explaining that the shrine bell rings for God but true devotion rings for the suffering, since showing mercy to the weak is the sweetest ring in the ear of the Lord, more than any ceremony.
bell, pity for the poor
The bell rings for the gods, but the hungry child's cry rings for the soul; answer the second.
doha on bell ringing vs helping the hungry
Every morning my neighbour rings the bell at her shrine and then turns away the hungry man outside, and I wonder about her religion.
cleric, show mercy
The cleric's call is heard by Heaven only when his own hand has first fed the starving.
doha on a cleric who is truly kind to the poor
Compose a doha about the cleric who gives bread to the hungry before he gives a sermon, showing that kindness to the suffering is the first duty of any who speak in the name of God.
Our cleric spends his evenings visiting sick families and the old, and his gentle visits matter more than all his lectures.

Compose a doha about those who put a lock on the poor and homeless as winter comes, and about the forest-dwelling saint who offers shelter to every stranger, showing that real religion is open-handed mercy.
I found a lock on the forest shelter where homeless people used to sleep, and I felt something should be said for such hard hearts.
doha on locks vs open hearts for the homeless, forest
lock, forest, open heart
The lock on the forest shelter is also a lock upon the owner's soul; mercy opens all.
The touchstone of religion is tenderness for the weak; all else is merely noise.
touchstone, mercy
doha on how kindness to the weak is the real test, touchstone of dharma
Write a doha showing that the touchstone of a person's goodness is how he treats those who cannot defend themselves, and that scriptures read without mercy are as empty as a meal without love.
I judge people by how they treat waiters and cleaners, and I wish I could have a doha about this touchstone.
My mother-in-law gave shelter to a stray family in the monsoon, even though we had little room, and said that is what being human means.
Open your arms to the shivering stranger; in his face you may meet the divine.
shelter the helpless

Please write a doha about how giving shelter, food and kindness to those in need, even when our own resources are limited, is the surest way to earn blessings and inner peace for the rest of one's life.
doha on helping strangers in need, even when you don't have much
doha on a parrot locked up, feeling sorry for it
I felt so much pity for the parrot in the neighbour's flat who never leaves its perch that I asked them to free it.
parrot, pity, freedom
The parrot in captivity speaks the words of its master, yet longs in silence for the open sky; pity it.
I'd like a doha about showing mercy to a parrot, which can speak but cannot choose its path, and about how pity for the voiceless is a sign of a noble and generous character.
Could you write a doha about how stars shine over everyone equally, and in the same way the kind person's tenderness falls on all under the sky as a tree gives shade to the weary?
stars, tree, tender heart
doha on a tree giving shade to the tired like pity for all
Under the stars, our village tree gave shelter to a sick traveller whom nobody would take, and the whole village talked of it for weeks.
The stars shine on all and the tree shelters all; so too the kind heart asks no one's name.
Be tender with the broken, for in their pain the Lord is nearest, and mercy is the surest prayer.
doha on being kind to sick people, my aunt is in hospital
mercy for the sick
My son gave his pocket money to a classmate who couldn't afford lunch, and I was proud and a little ashamed of myself.

Could you write a doha about how a person who shows mercy to the weak and the unwell receives more blessings than a hundred pilgrims, because tenderness toward the helpless is the very face of the divine?
prayer beads, pity
The beads may count a thousand names, but the hand that wipes a tear has prayed the best.
My grandmother counts her prayer beads for hours yet never helps the maid when she is ill, and I wish she would see the pity she owes.
Compose a doha showing that all the prayer beads one turns through the day are worthless if the heart is hard toward the poor and the sick, and that a single kind act beats a thousand chants.
doha on prayer beads vs real kindness to people in pain
Show mercy to the small, and the great will show mercy to you; for pity is a debt that is always repaid.
doha on being kind to people weaker than u

Please write a doha about how the strong show real greatness by protecting those weaker than themselves, not by crushing them, and how pity shown to the helpless returns as blessing in one's own hour of need.
protect the weak
When the school bully was crying after his parents' divorce, my daughter sat next to him and shared her snack, and that moved me deeply.
mountain, lamp, mercy
doha with a lamp on a mountain, kindness for a lost hiker

Write me a doha about the lamp that a kind villager keeps burning on the mountain path so that lost travellers can find shelter, showing that small acts of mercy can save lives and shine through the longest night.
On the mountain path a single lamp burns for the stranger; such is the light of a merciful soul.
Our village keeps a lamp lit at the foot of the mountain each night in case a lost hiker comes by, and it is the kindest tradition I know.
A bridge of mercy spans the gulf between rich and poor, and the swan crosses it with a gentle heart.
doha on swan and bridge for kindness to the weak
After the flood washed away the bridge, a farmer carried stranded children across on his back one by one, as gently as a swan.
bridge, swan, gentle pity

Write a doha about the swan that glides across the water with a gentle spirit and the bridge that links the poor to the rich, both teaching that mercy is the road on which the weak and strong may meet.
The yogi lays down his meditation to bind the wound of a stranger; the moth burns, but mercy gives light.
My yogi friend once cut short his meditation to help a stray puppy hit by a vehicle, while a moth fluttered above his head, and I remember it still.
doha on a yogi who stops meditating to help someone in pain
yogi, moth, pity
Compose a doha showing that the true yogi is not one who sits unmoved in meditation while the moth struggles nearby, but one who rises to help every suffering creature without waiting to be asked.
Write a doha about how a ruler without mercy has no real kingdom, while a poor man who shares his last meal with a stranger rules the world, because pity enriches and cruelty impoverishes.
rule with mercy
doha on rulers who are kind vs cruel
Power is heavy without tenderness; the poor man's mercy is lighter than any royal command.
The old village head always put the poorest family's needs before his own, and when he died, the whole district wept for him.

Could you write a doha for my friend who volunteers at a shelter for abandoned animals and sick elderly alike, reminding him that kindness to the weak is the highest religion and that he walks the right path?
My friend gives his weekends to the old and abandoned at the shelter, and I wish to tell him in a doha that this is the real religion.
doha for a volunteer who helps the old and sick
Blessed are the hands that tend the lonely; they carry the weight of Heaven's own love.
tend the helpless
doha on a sweet tongue and salt in the wound: how cruelty hurts and pity heals

Please write a doha about how a harsh tongue is like salt on an open wound while a gentle word of comfort is a healing balm, showing that compassion for the afflicted begins with the way we speak to them.
salt, tongue, tenderness
Salt on the wound is the cruel tongue; the kind word is balm, and the gentle are comforters.
When my friend was crying after her loss, my aunt's sharp tongue added salt to the wound, but a stranger's gentle word helped her.
We walked through the forest with prayer beads and chanting, and passed a lost child crying; it was a stranger who stopped, not the pilgrims.
forest, prayer beads, pity
doha on pilgrims who ignore a crying kid, forest, prayer beads

Write a doha about the pilgrim who walks through the forest chanting on his prayer beads but passes by a crying child without stopping, showing that rituals are empty when kindness to the suffering is forgotten.
Through the forest the pilgrim chants and counts his beads; yet the crying child is left behind, and the Lord with him.
doha on being kind to ppl at work who are struggling

Could you write a doha that says the world is full of silent sufferers whom we pass every day, and a person who learns to see their pain and respond with warmth has found the greatest treasure of life?
Look closely at each face that passes by; behind its quiet is a sorrow waiting for a kind word.
A junior at work was crying in the stairwell, and instead of ignoring it, I asked if she wanted tea, and she poured her heart out.
see their pain

We left the cremation ground that evening after the funeral of a poor man whose family could not afford a thing, and a neighbour quietly handed them an envelope with the one-string lute player's earnings.
cremation ground, lute, pity
Compose a doha about the lute player who plays at the cremation ground for a poor man's funeral without taking a coin, showing that mercy for the grieving is the music God loves most.
doha on kindness at a poor persons cremation ground, one-string lute
At the cremation ground the lute cries with the bereaved, and the tender-hearted give what they can.
One thread of mercy mends a torn life; stitch the wounded to the world with kindness.
thread, pity for the poor

Please compose a doha about how a single thread of kindness can mend the torn lives of the poor and abandoned, and how the people who hold the thread and refuse to give it have not understood their own humanity.
doha on a little thread of kindness to help the poor
My aunt always carries thread to mend the clothes of poor children at the roadside school, and that small kindness changes their whole day.
doha on a potter who gives free pots to the poor, plus sandalwood vibes

Could you write a doha about the potter who shapes clay for the poor and charges them nothing, and about the sandalwood-like fragrance that such quiet generosity leaves on the street long after he is gone?
potter, sandalwood, kind giving
The potter shapes the clay for the poor with love, and the fragrance of sandalwood follows his gentle hands.
The old potter in our lane lets poor families take his pots free, and his reputation smells sweeter than sandalwood in our colony.
doha on how a fire burns everyone's hut, we should help those who lost everything
When fire swept the slum last month, my neighbours who barely had anything opened their small rooms to the families who lost everything.
Please compose a doha about how a fire in the village leaves the poor without shelter or food, and how the kindness of those who give them a place and a meal is the greatest religion of all.
When fire devours the poor man's roof, it is the open hand of a neighbour that rebuilds his hope.
fire victims, help them
The jaggery of kindness sweetens the moneylender's heart, and he who gives it out among the poor is richer than any stored treasure.
jaggery, moneylender, mercy
The moneylender in our town forgave a poor widow's debt and handed her jaggery to sweeten the news, and she wept with gratitude.
doha on a moneylender who shows mercy and forgives a debt

Please write a doha about the moneylender who burns the loan papers of a destitute family and shares jaggery with the children, showing that compassion turns even a lender of money into a giver of blessings.
At the wedding, the palanquin passed a wounded elephant by the road, and the groom got down to look after it before going on to the ceremony.
Compose a doha about a groom who steps down from his palanquin to help a hurt elephant, delaying his own wedding, showing that kindness to a suffering creature is the best sign of a noble man.
He left the palanquin to comfort the wounded elephant, and in that mercy the whole wedding was blessed.
doha on groom stopping his doli to help an injured elephant
palanquin, elephant, mercy
In the temple of the heart let mercy be the first guest and the last; no idol pleases like a tender soul.
doha on temple visit, but helping poor ppl outside more important
temple, mercy first
Outside the temple a crowd stood for darshan while a sick old man lay unnoticed on the steps, and only one boy stopped to give him a drink.

Write a doha about how worship inside the temple is meaningless when one passes by the sick and hungry at its steps, since the Lord is more pleased by a cup of water given to the thirsty than by flowers.
doha on a sword that protects the weak vs one that hurts them
My brother-in-law, a soldier with a sword on his wall, once stopped a street gang from beating up a stranger, and he never talks about it.
Please write a doha showing that the true use of a sword is to defend the weak and not to bully them, and that a warrior who spares the helpless is nobler than a thousand who conquer through fear.
sword, protect the helpless
The sword is blessed only in the hand that shields the weak; in cruel hands it is a curse.
A girl in my class was being teased about her accent, and I sat beside her at lunch without making a big deal of it, and I could see how much it meant to her.
Sit beside the lonely one; your presence is a mercy that no wealth can buy.
doha on standing by a kid who is being bullied

Write me a doha about how a small act of kindness to a lonely or ridiculed person, a seat offered or a smile shared, can change a life, and how pity is not weakness but the beginning of true strength.
stand by the lonely
I want a doha about how a person who has seen suffering learns to feel for others, and how any faith or nation that forgets the poor, the sick and the old has forgotten the first law of dharma.
After I spent a month in hospital, I started noticing how lonely the other patients were, and now I visit them every week.
He who has once been wounded knows how to bind another's pain, and in that knowing lives the root of mercy.
kindness to patients
doha on how suffering teaches us to care for others

Compose a doha showing that gentleness toward the helpless is the surest sign of a great soul, that the strong show their worth when they bend toward the weak, and that no charity beats real tenderness.
Greatness bows to the lowly, as the strong bend to the child; this is the mark of mercy.
tenderness to the helpless
doha on being gentle with weak ppl
My father, though strict, was always gentle with the poor and street kids, and I now think that was the best part of his character.
potter, jaggery, kindness
Compose a doha about how a poor potter who sells his clay pots for a pittance still shares his jaggery with the poorest children of the lane, showing that mercy needs no riches, only a loving heart.
doha on a potter who gives jaggery to the poor children
The potter in our lane gives every poor child a lump of jaggery after school, and he has never asked anything in return.
The potter's hands are rough with clay, yet he offers jaggery to hungry children, and sweetness fills his poor lane.

Could you write a doha about the thief who stole in the night but returned after seeing the dew-soaked starving family, leaving food for them, showing that even a hardened heart can melt in the face of real suffering?
dew, thief, soft heart
One dewy morning a man who had come to steal from our poor neighbours ended up leaving some of his own food on their step.
The dew falls gently on the sleeping poor, and even the thief cannot steal from their sorrow.
doha on a thief who felt pity and left food

Write a doha showing that the religion of a family is in how it treats the stranger who knocks at midnight and the poor who arrive empty-handed, and that every refusal is a rejection of dharma itself.
kindness to strangers
doha on being nice to strangers who need help
Welcome the stranger in the night, for mercy opens before the knock.
A stranger knocked at our place at midnight asking for water during the rain, and my mother let him in and fed him, and I never forgot it.
My uncle, who is a musk deer breeder, gave a philosopher's stone-shaped paperweight to a poor student, saying one's kindness matters more than any gift.
doha with a musk deer and philosopher's stone about pity
musk deer, philosopher's stone, mercy

Compose a doha showing that a musk deer's scent and the philosopher's stone's touch are nothing compared to the transforming power of mercy, which turns the heart of the cruel into gentleness and riches into ordinary dust.
The musk deer bears fragrance, the philosopher's stone makes treasure, but mercy turns the very soul to light.
At the crossroads of life let the kind soul stand, offering water and direction to all who are lost.
Last week at a busy crossroads a blind old man wanted to cross, and a schoolgirl took his hand without being asked.
doha on kind ppl at crossroads helping lost ppl
crossroads, kindness

Please write a doha about the person who stands at the crossroads and gives water, directions and a kind word to every lost soul without asking their name, and who thereby earns a place among the blessed.
The bell calls the faithful to pray, yet the rainbird's thirst is answered only by a merciful hand.
When the bell rang for evening prayer in our lane, I saw an old man give a drink to the thirsty rainbird in his courtyard before he went to pray.
Compose a doha about how the sound of the bell calls people to worship but the cry of a thirsty rainbird calls us to mercy, and the one who answers the cry has already answered the bell.
doha on bell and rainbird, pity for a thirsty creature
bell, rainbird, mercy
salt, mercy
Salt of tears, salt of toil; give the poor a loaf to ease their burden and mercy will season your own days.
doha on sharing salt and bread with the hungry
Our cook gives a pinch of salt and a warm roti to any hungry stranger who stops by, and she says that is her daily prayer.

Please write a doha about how a little salt and a morsel of bread shared with the hungry stranger is worth more than a feast eaten alone, because mercy shared is the only meal that nourishes the soul.
Let your tenderness reach those who have no one; the lonely are God's own guests.
My neighbour is a widow with no children, and I have started to take her out every week, because someone must care.
Could you write a doha about the loneliness of the old and the widowed and about how a visit, a call or a meal brought to them is a gift greater than anything money can buy?
doha on visiting lonely old ppl
care for the lonely
Where there is mercy, the cold of the world melts; let the weeping find a gentle ear.

Please write a doha about the way kindness warms the cold hours of a suffering person's life, and about how one who listens without judging and helps without being asked has already fulfilled the whole law.
listen to sorrow
When my friend lost her baby, I did not say anything wise, I just sat beside her for hours and held her hand.
doha on just being there for someone who is hurting
At the bier the grindstone of grief grinds all alike; give your mercy to the mourners while they weep.
doha on bier and grindstone, helping poor families at funerals
bier, grindstone, mercy

Compose a doha showing that when a poor man's bier is lifted and his family is crushed by grief as by a grindstone, the neighbour who stands beside them with food and kindness has performed the greatest religion.
When the poor tailor died and his bier was carried out, the whole street gathered what little they had to help his widow, who ground flour all day to feed her children at the grindstone.
mosque, cotton, kindness
Write a doha about the volunteer who leaves the mosque each Friday to hand out cotton blankets to the poor, and teaches that real prayer is the warmth you give to others when the cold winds blow.
doha on a mosque giving cotton blankets to the poor in winter
Our local mosque collects cotton quilts every winter for families who have none, and the quiet kindness of it moves me every year.
From the mosque comes the call to prayer, and from soft cotton comes the answer of mercy to the shivering poor.
The blind man asks for no sight, only a kind hand; give it, and you will see the face of God.
doha on helping a blind man cross the road
I watched a young boy gently lead a blind man across a busy street and refuse any reward, and I wanted to write a verse about it.
help the blind man
Please compose a doha about how guiding a blind man with patience and respect is better than a hundred sermons, since mercy to those who cannot see is the clearest vision a person can achieve.
Could you write a doha about the cloud that rains alike on the good and the wicked, the rich and the poor, as a picture of how mercy ought to fall on everyone without asking who deserves it?
After the rains the whole village shared its food with the families whose fields were flooded, and nobody asked who was rich or poor.
doha on clouds raining on everyone like kindness
cloud, mercy for all
The cloud asks not whose field is parched, and pours its mercy on every thirsty ground.
doha on giving a pot of water to a thirsty stranger
On a hot afternoon I offered a pot of water to a tired labourer on the road, and the blessing in his eyes was worth everything.
A pot of water offered to the thirsty, in the heat of noon, has washed away a thousand sins.
pot of water, kindness
Write a doha about how a simple pot of water offered to a thirsty passer-by in the heat of summer is the cheapest and most precious charity, a deed that brings the giver more joy than a feast.
A man in my neighbourhood noticed a schoolchild without lunch each day, and quietly started leaving food for him without ever saying a word.
Quiet is the mercy that leaves a gift unsigned, and blessed is the hand that gives and hides.
doha on secretly helping someone in need
silent kindness

Write a doha about doing good to the helpless in secret, expecting neither thanks nor praise, because mercy performed for show is vanity, while mercy performed in silence is worship that reaches the Lord.
